Laguna Beach.decision: approved (ministerial design review + coastal development permit, unanimous); parcel map recommended to Council
Laguna Beach.summary: Commission used SB 4 (Affordable Housing on Faith and Higher Education Lands Act) to approve a three-story building with 28 deed-restricted lower-income units plus a manager unit and a 41-stall garage on the church's parking lot. It forwarded the four-lots-to-two parcel map to City Council.

Laguna Beach.project: Neighborhood Congregational Church Affordable Housing (Related California)
Laguna Beach.summary: Council committed $6.71M from restricted funds, waivers and deferrals to the 29-unit, 100% affordable project on church-leased land (9 ELI, 3 VLI, 16 LI units). Reported by LB Indy on 2026-07-17; exact meeting date not stated.

La Habra.project: Diocese of Orange apartments at Our Lady of Guadalupe Catholic Church
issues: did not use SB 4 or density bonus
La Habra.summary: Council approved 21 mostly market-rate apartments on a 1.6-acre church field, with two units affordable to moderate-income tenants. Affordable-housing advocates criticized the Diocese for not using SB 4 or a density bonus (reported 2025-03-24).

Yorba Linda.project: Solana Walk townhomes on Messiah Lutheran Church parking lot (Olson Urban Housing)
Yorba Linda.decision: land sold; proceeding under Congregational Overlay Zone
Yorba Linda.summary: Olson bought the church's 1.9-acre parking lot to build 40 three-story townhomes; 8 will be sold to moderate-income households by lottery with 45-year restrictions. Built under Yorba Linda's Congregational Overlay Zone (reported 2026-06-08).

Fullerton.project: Church-site SB 4 housing concept (downtown housing sites study)
Fullerton.decision: study accepted; staff directed to advance sites (4-1)
issues: not shown to community or Planning Commission first (dissenting vote)
Fullerton.summary: Study concept puts up to 36 homes behind the church with a new church lot replacing a lawn by Gilbert Park; under SB 4 it would be 100% affordable with no CEQA review. Owner had approached the city about housing.

Fullerton.project: City-owned lot next to Fullerton Transportation Center
Fullerton.decision: prioritized; staff to start Surplus Land Act process (4-1)
issues: industrial zoning must change to mixed-use
shared parking agreement with SoCo garage
Fullerton.summary: Council chose this empty city lot as the first site to pursue, starting Surplus Land Act paperwork, rezoning and title review before requesting developer proposals. It can use the nearby SoCo parking garage instead of new parking.

Fullerton.decision: studied; costs to be determined before seeking developers
issues: needs smaller units and reduced parking
Fullerton.summary: Study found strong housing potential but an existing parking structure adds cost. Recommendation is to price demolition and utility moves before soliciting developers.

Santa Ana.project: Habitat for Humanity of Orange County duplexes
Santa Ana.summary: Council funded six 3-bed, 2-bath for-sale homes in three duplexes for households up to 80% AMI with a Santa Ana live/work preference. Predates 2024 but is the base record for this site; completion was projected for December 2024.

Santa Ana.project: Habitat for Humanity of Orange County Alton Avenue homes
Santa Ana.summary: A public petition backs Habitat's proposed 40 affordable for-sale homes at this address. The city staff report on its funding could not be read (Santa Ana's Laserfiche portal needs JavaScript), so no vote or amount is recorded here.

Costa Mesa.project: Mesa Motel conversion on Harbor Boulevard
issues: concern it is supportive housing rather than workforce housing
Costa Mesa.summary: Commission approved converting the defunct 1958 Mesa Motel into 47 single-room units for very-low-income residents, with priority for veterans, seniors and people with disabilities. One commissioner said it read like a supportive-housing motel conversion.

Westminster.body: City of Westminster (Notice of Exemption filed)
Westminster.summary: 89 condominiums on 3.62 acres replacing a 37,092 sq ft commercial building; 9 units deed-restricted for low-income households earn a 20% density bonus. Date is the CEQA notice filing date.

Fountain Valley.summary: 18-acre former strawberry field approved for 304 market-rate apartments, 83 affordable senior units, and 219 for-sale townhomes and triplexes. Reported 2025-07-15; for-sale phases expected 2028-2029.

issues: Council considered appealing Planning Commission approval
Fountain Valley.summary: Council signed the affordable housing agreement for the 83 senior affordable units despite pushback from residents and the mayor. Members said fighting state housing law would be costly and likely lost (reported 2025-11-20).

Lake Forest.summary: Council approved a $4.35M loan for a four-story, 50-unit affordable project, the city's first by-right project. It is paid mostly with in-lieu fees collected from developers who skipped on-site affordable units.

Mission Viejo.project: Vista Del Lago apartments expansion off Marguerite Parkway
Mission Viejo.decision: recommended for approval; Council hearing set for March 10
Mission Viejo.summary: Plan demolishes 68 units and builds 418 (net 350 new) with 53 affordable units (27 low, 26 very-low income) on a 33-acre site. Commissioners said state law left them little discretion; year not stated on the page.

Buena Park.project: Townhomes at southeast corner of Dale Street and La Palma Avenue
Buena Park.summary: Council approved redeveloping an old commercial property into 93 townhomes including 14 affordable units. Part of a Buena Park push to put housing on aging commercial sites.

Huntington Beach.summary: After years of fighting state mandates, Council reluctantly approved a housing plan in June 2026 to avoid escalating fines. The mayor said 13,000+ new units would hurt residents, citing parking.
